text: Your wobbly tooth finally comes out in an apple. {mother} says to put it under your pillow tonight.

choices.label: Put it under the pillow
choices.outcome: In the morning there was a shiny coin and a tiny note in very familiar handwriting.

choices.label: Stay awake to catch the tooth fairy
choices.outcome: You lasted until 9:14pm. The coin appeared anyway. The mystery deepens.

choices.label: Keep the tooth in a box
choices.outcome: You now own a small, slightly gross treasure. You check on it regularly.

text: Swimming lessons start this week. The pool smells of chlorine and everyone else seems to already know how to float.

choices.label: Jump straight in
choices.outcome: You swallowed half the pool and came up grinning. By the end of term you could swim a length.

choices.label: Cling to the side
choices.outcome: You held the edge for three weeks, then let go one day without noticing. Now you can swim.

choices.label: Fake a tummy ache
choices.outcome: You sat on the bench in a towel every week. You still cannot swim.

text: You have a new best friend called Captain Biscuit. Nobody else can see him, which is very convenient for him.

choices.label: Set a place for him at dinner
choices.outcome: {parent} played along and passed Captain Biscuit the peas. He did not eat them either.

choices.label: Blame him for the broken vase
choices.outcome: Captain Biscuit got a stern talking-to. So did you.

text: The class trip is to the natural history museum. There is a dinosaur skeleton the size of a bus and a gift shop the size of a dream.

choices.label: Fill in the whole worksheet
choices.outcome: You learned that some dinosaurs had feathers and told everyone for a month.

choices.label: Spend your money in the gift shop
choices.outcome: You came home with a rubber T. rex and a pencil shaped like a bone. Worth it.

choices.label: Get lost on purpose
choices.outcome: You found a quiet room full of beetles. A guard found you. The teacher was not amused.

text: {parent} wheels out a bike with a bow on the handlebars. The stabilisers are coming off today.

choices.label: Let them run behind you
choices.outcome: They let go without telling you. You were halfway down the street before you noticed. You were flying.

choices.label: Insist on doing it alone
choices.outcome: You fell off eleven times and got back on twelve.

text: It is your turn to take the class guinea pig, Professor Nibbles, home for the weekend.

choices.label: Look after him perfectly
choices.outcome: You wrote a diary of his weekend with drawings. The teacher put it on the wall.

choices.label: Teach him tricks
choices.outcome: Professor Nibbles learned nothing. You learned patience.

choices.label: Let him explore the house
choices.outcome: He was found on Sunday night inside a slipper. Everyone aged ten years.

text: A poster in the corridor: CHESS CLUB, Tuesdays, biscuits provided.

choices.label: Join for the chess
choices.outcome: You lost every game for a month, then won one. You have been hooked ever since.

choices.label: Join for the biscuits
choices.outcome: You never learned how the horse moves, but the biscuits were excellent.

choices.label: Walk past
choices.outcome: You never found out if you would have been good at it.

text: Your grandmother pulls out an old photo album and starts telling you about the year she ran away to join a dance troupe.

choices.label: Ask a hundred questions
choices.outcome: You heard about the train, the tour and the boy with the trumpet. You will tell your own grandchildren one day.

choices.label: Say it sounds made up
choices.outcome: She laughed and closed the album. You wish now you had let her finish.

text: The neighbours ask if you would babysit their twins on Saturday. Ten dollars an hour and all the pizza you can eat.

choices.label: Say yes and take it seriously
choices.outcome: The twins were angels for you, which nobody believed. They asked for you every weekend after that.

choices.label: Say yes and invite friends round
choices.outcome: The twins told on you within the hour. You were not asked back.

choices.label: Say no
choices.outcome: You kept your Saturday. The pizza went to someone else.

text: {friend} wants to start a band. They have a name (The Wet Socks), a logo and absolutely no songs.

choices.label: Learn the drums
choices.outcome: Your family bought earplugs. After a year you were actually good.

choices.label: Write the lyrics
choices.outcome: Your first song was about a bus. It was surprisingly moving.

choices.label: Be their manager
choices.outcome: You booked one gig at a cafe. Six people came. It was glorious.

text: The Wet Socks have their first real gig, at a pub with a sticky floor and a sound engineer who hates you.

choices.label: Play your hearts out
choices.outcome: The crowd of eleven people cheered for an encore. You did not have another song, so you played the first one again.

choices.label: Freeze on stage
choices.outcome: You stood still for the whole set. Someone said it was "very avant-garde".

text: Final exams are in three weeks. Your desk is buried in notes and you have started dreaming in equations.

choices.label: Make a timetable and stick to it
choices.outcome: It was boring and it worked. You walked into the hall calm.

choices.label: Cram the night before
choices.outcome: You knew everything at 3am and nothing at 9am.

choices.label: Revise with friends
choices.outcome: You learned half as much and laughed twice as much. Your grades were fine.

text: The animal shelter needs volunteers on Saturdays to walk dogs and clean cages.

choices.label: Sign up
choices.outcome: You walked a three-legged greyhound called Rocket every week. He was the fastest dog there.

choices.label: Sign up for the certificate
choices.outcome: You went four times and put it on your CV in large letters.

choices.label: Sleep in instead
choices.outcome: Your Saturdays stayed yours.

text: Your driving instructor grips the dashboard as you approach a roundabout at a speed best described as optimistic.

choices.label: Slow down and listen
choices.outcome: You went round twice, signalled properly and the instructor breathed again.

choices.label: Keep your foot down
choices.outcome: You made it round. The instructor added three extra lessons to your plan.

text: School is over. Before anything else, you could take a year to travel, work or just think.

choices.label: Backpack around the world ($3,000)
choices.outcome: Hostels, night buses, one stolen phone and a hundred stories.

choices.label: Work and save
choices.outcome: A year of shifts. You started the next chapter with money in the bank.

choices.label: Go straight on
choices.outcome: No pause. You kept your momentum.

text: Your flatmate has started eating your food, borrowing your clothes and leaving the hob on.

choices.label: Have an honest talk
choices.outcome: It was awkward for exactly four minutes, then much better.

choices.label: Label everything passive-aggressively
choices.outcome: Your yoghurt now says "MINE (please)". It has not helped.

choices.label: Move out
choices.outcome: You found a smaller place with a door that locks. Peace.

text: Your first proper payslip arrives. There is a big number at the top and a smaller one at the bottom.

choices.label: Learn what every deduction means
choices.outcome: Tax, pension, insurance. You now understand more than most adults.

choices.label: Treat yourself ($300)
choices.outcome: You bought something you did not need and loved it.

choices.label: Save half of it
choices.outcome: It felt boring. It was the smartest thing you did that year.

text: {friend} is getting married on a beach on the other side of the world. The invitation is beautiful. The flights are not.

choices.label: Go ($2,500)
choices.outcome: You cried during the vows and danced barefoot until the sun came up.

choices.label: Send a generous gift instead
choices.outcome: They understood, mostly. The photos looked incredible.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.outcome: {friend} said it was fine. It was slightly less than fine.

text: Everyone you know seems to have a side hustle. You have a skill, an evening free and a vague plan.

choices.label: Start one
choices.outcome: You sold handmade things online. It paid for your holidays.

choices.label: Rest instead
choices.outcome: Your evenings stayed quiet. You slept better than everyone with a hustle.

text: {friend} asks you to give a speech at their engagement party. Tomorrow.

choices.label: Write something heartfelt
choices.outcome: Half the room cried. The other half pretended they had something in their eye.

choices.label: Wing it with embarrassing stories
choices.outcome: Big laughs, one gasp, and a long look from {friend}'s new in-laws.

text: Your home feels a bit bare. The plant shop down the road has a sale on.

choices.label: Buy a whole jungle ($120)
choices.outcome: Twenty plants. Eighteen survived. You talk to them now.

choices.label: Buy one cactus
choices.outcome: It is still alive. It may outlive you.

text: You wake up at 3am convinced everyone else has their life figured out and you are falling behind.

choices.label: Talk to someone about it
choices.outcome: It turned out nearly everyone feels like this. That helped more than you expected.

choices.label: Make a big change
choices.outcome: You signed up for something new the next morning. Terrifying and exciting.

choices.label: Scroll until dawn
choices.outcome: Everyone online looked happier. They were not.

text: Your building is voting on whether to ban bikes from the hallway. The meeting is tonight and feelings are high.

choices.label: Go and speak up
choices.outcome: You proposed a bike rack. It passed unanimously. You are now on the committee.

choices.label: Stay home
choices.outcome: The ban passed. Your bike lives in your kitchen now.

text: You invited people round for dinner and the main course is on fire. Literally.

choices.label: Order pizza and laugh it off
choices.outcome: Everyone agreed it was the best dinner party they had been to.

choices.label: Serve it anyway
choices.outcome: You called it "blackened". Nobody believed you, but they ate it.

text: Your suitcase did not arrive. The airline's app says it is "in transit", which could mean anywhere.

choices.label: Stay calm and file a claim
choices.outcome: It turned up two days later with a new sticker from a country you have never visited.

choices.label: Buy a whole new wardrobe ($400)
choices.outcome: Holiday you has much better taste than regular you.

text: Your team throws you a surprise party for five years at the company. There is a cake with your face printed on it.

choices.label: Give a little speech
choices.outcome: You thanked everyone by name. Even the quiet guy from IT smiled.

choices.label: Eat your own face
choices.outcome: You took the first slice, from the forehead. Legendary.

text: Your boss asks you to represent the company at a conference abroad. Three days, a hotel and a lanyard.

choices.label: Network like mad
choices.outcome: You came back with forty business cards and one real friend.

choices.label: Sneak off to see the city
choices.outcome: You missed one talk and saw the most beautiful cathedral of your life.

choices.label: Stay in the hotel
choices.outcome: Room service, crisp sheets and twelve hours of sleep. Bliss.

text: An envelope goes round the office for someone's birthday. You have no idea who they are.

choices.label: Put in $10 and sign it warmly
choices.outcome: They thanked you in the kitchen later. Now you know who they are.

choices.label: Pass it on quickly
choices.outcome: Nobody noticed. Probably.

text: A nervous new starter keeps asking you questions. Your manager suggests you mentor them.

choices.label: Take them under your wing
choices.outcome: Two years later they got promoted and thanked you in their speech.

choices.label: Point them to the manual
choices.outcome: They figured it out eventually, without you.

text: The new neighbours throw a loud party until 2am on a Tuesday.

choices.label: Knock and join in
choices.outcome: You ended up dancing in their kitchen. You are best friends now.

choices.label: Knock and complain politely
choices.outcome: They apologised with a bottle of wine the next day.

choices.label: Lie awake fuming
choices.outcome: You did not sleep. You did compose a very strongly worded note.

text: The bus you are on makes a noise like a dying goose and stops on the hard shoulder. Everyone looks at each other.

choices.label: Organise a group taxi
choices.outcome: You split a minibus with six strangers. By the time you arrived you had a new friend and a recipe for soup.

choices.label: Wait it out with a book
choices.outcome: The replacement bus came two hours later. You finished the book.

text: You come home to find the back door open. Nothing seems to be missing, but the drawers have been searched.

choices.label: Change the locks ($300)
choices.outcome: New locks, new alarm, and you finally sleep through the night again.

choices.label: Get a big dog
choices.outcome: Your new dog is enormous and terrified of the hoover. Burglars do not know that.

choices.label: Shrug it off
choices.outcome: You jumped at every noise for a month.

text: {parent} retires after forty years in the same job. There is a party with cheese on sticks and a very emotional speech.

choices.label: Give a toast
choices.outcome: You told the story about the day they took you to work. Everyone cried.

choices.label: Help them plan their new life
choices.outcome: They signed up for pottery, Spanish and a choir in one week. You created a monster.

text: {partner} has a bad case of flu and is being very dramatic about it.

choices.label: Bring soup and sympathy
choices.outcome: You made soup, fetched blankets and watched their favourite films. They will never forget it.

choices.label: Leave them to rest
choices.outcome: They survived. They mention it occasionally.

text: {partner} hands you an envelope: two tickets for a weekend away, leaving tomorrow.

choices.label: Pack in ten minutes
choices.outcome: A tiny hotel, long walks and the best conversation you have had in years.

choices.label: Say you cannot get time off
choices.outcome: They went with their sister instead. It stung.

text: {child} has been cast as "Tree Number Three" in the school play and is taking it extremely seriously.

choices.label: Sit in the front row
choices.outcome: Tree Number Three did not move a single branch. You clapped louder than anyone.

choices.label: Miss it for work
choices.outcome: {child} looked for you in the audience. You were not there.

text: {child} asks, very seriously, where people go when they die.

choices.label: Answer honestly and gently
choices.outcome: You talked for an hour. They hugged you and asked for a snack.

choices.label: Change the subject to ice cream
choices.outcome: It worked, for now. The question will come back.

text: The school calls. {child} was caught skipping class to go to the arcade.

choices.label: Talk, then ground them
choices.outcome: They sulked for a week, then told you what was really going on. You are glad you listened.

choices.label: Shout
choices.outcome: The door slammed. Again.

choices.label: Secretly admire their nerve
choices.outcome: You hid a smile, then made them write an apology.

text: {child} graduates today. You are in the third row with a camera and a tissue.

choices.label: Cheer embarrassingly loudly
choices.outcome: They pretended to be mortified. The photo of their face is your favourite.

choices.label: Take everyone out to dinner ($300)
choices.outcome: A long table, too much food and a toast to the future.

text: You realise you have not learned anything new just for fun in years.

choices.label: Take up pottery
choices.outcome: Your first bowl is the shape of a sad hat. You love it.

choices.label: Learn a language
choices.outcome: You can now order coffee and apologise in Italian.

choices.label: Start running
choices.outcome: You ran a 5k by summer. Your knees have opinions.

text: You hold the menu further and further away until your arms run out.

choices.label: Get glasses
choices.outcome: You can read again. You also look very distinguished.

choices.label: Refuse to admit it
choices.outcome: You ordered the wrong dish three times this month.

text: A message from someone you have not spoken to since school: "Is this really you? I have thought about you so often."

choices.label: Meet for coffee
choices.outcome: Three hours later you were still laughing about the chemistry teacher. It was like no time had passed.

choices.label: Reply politely and leave it
choices.outcome: Some memories are better as memories.

text: After a relative's funeral, the family argues about who gets the silver tea set. Voices are being raised over the sandwiches.

choices.label: Step back and keep the peace
choices.outcome: You took nothing and kept your family. You think that was the better inheritance.

choices.label: Fight for what is fair
choices.outcome: You got the tea set. Your cousin has not spoken to you since.

text: Your home feels too big now. Every room has a memory and a pile of things nobody uses.

choices.label: Clear it out room by room
choices.outcome: You found letters, drawings and a box of photos. It took a year and it was worth it.

choices.label: Leave it all as it is
choices.outcome: The memories stay where they are.

text: The bank has closed its branch and everything is an app now.

choices.label: Ask a young relative to teach you
choices.outcome: Three lessons and a lot of patience later, you can send money and voice notes.

choices.label: Work it out yourself
choices.outcome: It took a weekend and some language, but you got there.

choices.label: Refuse on principle
choices.outcome: You now take two buses to the nearest branch. Principles are expensive.

text: Your old friends have a standing lunch on the first Monday of the month. There are fewer of you every year.

choices.label: Never miss one
choices.outcome: You laugh more on those Mondays than the rest of the month together.

choices.label: Go when you can
choices.outcome: It is always lovely when you do.

text: The village garden show is next month and your marrows are looking competitive.

choices.label: Enter everything
choices.outcome: Second place for marrows, first place for sweet peas. A triumph.

choices.label: Enter just the roses
choices.outcome: Highly commended. You framed the certificate.

choices.label: Judge quietly from the sidelines
choices.outcome: You had opinions about every entry.

text: {child} asks if you would record your life story so the family never loses it.

choices.label: Record every story
choices.outcome: Twelve hours of tapes, three of them about one disastrous camping trip.

choices.label: Pick the best ones
choices.outcome: One evening, one cup of tea, ten stories. Enough.

text: {grandchild} wants to sleep over at yours and has packed a bag with nine teddies and no pyjamas.

choices.label: Build a blanket fort
choices.outcome: You stayed up past your bedtime telling stories by torchlight.

choices.label: Early night for everyone
choices.outcome: They were asleep by eight. You were asleep by eight-oh-five.

text: {grandchild} has a school project: interview the oldest person you know. That is apparently you.

choices.label: Tell them everything
choices.outcome: They got an A. You got a framed copy of the project.

choices.label: Make it more exciting than it was
choices.outcome: In their version you fought a bear. The teacher had questions.

text: {grandchild} decides you need to learn a dance from the internet.

choices.label: Learn it properly
choices.outcome: You nailed it. The video has been watched by the whole family forty times.

choices.label: Watch from the sofa
choices.outcome: You clapped. That counted.

text: {grandchild} calls to say they got their first job. They wanted you to be the first to know.

choices.label: Send a card with a little money
choices.outcome: They framed the card and spent the money on pizza for the team.

choices.label: Give them your best work advice
choices.outcome: They wrote it down. All of it.

text: It is late and the house is quiet, but you can hear crying from the foster room.

choices.label: Sit outside their door and talk softly
choices.outcome: You talked about nothing for an hour. Eventually the crying stopped and a small voice said "goodnight".

choices.label: Make hot chocolate for two
choices.outcome: You sat at the kitchen table at midnight, not saying much. It was a start.

text: A letter arrives in handwriting you do not recognise. It is from a child you once fostered, all grown up now.

choices.label: Write back straight away
choices.outcome: They are doing well. They said the year with you was when things started getting better.

choices.label: Read it again and again
choices.outcome: You keep it in your bedside drawer.

text: Another collector at the fair wants the exact same item you do. They have deep pockets and no shame.

choices.label: Outbid them ($500)
choices.outcome: You won. They glared. It was worth every penny.

choices.label: Let them have it and befriend them
choices.outcome: You swapped numbers and now trade tips. Rivals make good friends.

text: A relative tells you the real story behind the family heirloom, and it is nothing like the version you grew up with.

choices.label: Write the true story down
choices.outcome: Now it will be passed on with the heirloom, warts and all.

choices.label: Keep the old version
choices.outcome: Some stories are better as legends.

text: Your elderly neighbour has not collected their post for three days.

choices.label: Knock and check on them
choices.outcome: They had a fall and could not reach the phone. You may have saved their life.

choices.label: Assume they are away
choices.outcome: An ambulance came on the fourth day. You wish you had knocked.

text: A colleague is running a marathon for charity and the sponsor form is on your desk.

choices.label: Sponsor generously ($100)
choices.outcome: They finished in five hours and thanked you in an emotional group email.

choices.label: Sponsor a little ($10)
choices.outcome: Every bit helps.

choices.label: Pretend you did not see it
choices.outcome: It stayed on your desk for a week, judging you.

text: Your body is telling you something: you have been running on coffee and four hours of sleep for months.

choices.label: Take a proper week off
choices.outcome: You slept, walked and read. You came back sharper than ever.

choices.label: Push through
choices.outcome: You pushed through. Something gave in March.

text: Your usual lottery numbers came up this week. You did not buy a ticket this week.

choices.label: Laugh about it
choices.outcome: It became your best story at parties.

choices.label: Never buy a ticket again
choices.outcome: You have saved hundreds since. Small comfort.

text: You go back to the street where you grew up. The house is a different colour and the corner shop is a phone repair place.

choices.label: Knock on your old door
choices.outcome: The new owners showed you round. Your height marks were still on the kitchen doorframe.

choices.label: Just walk past
choices.outcome: Some places are better kept in memory.
